content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification:** deviation (fallback target).

The only licence to us is § 23.4's escrow source-code licence, which is "non-transferable," runs only through the end of the Term, and names only "Customer." Neither fallback element is met: § 21.10/§ 21.11(A) address processing Services for Affiliates (not licence scope), § 22.4's merger carve-out covers assignment of the Agreement rather than the licence, and § 23.5(1) independently bars transfer or assignment of the source code to any third party.

**Cure (two surgical replaces):**
1. § 23.4 — grant extended to Customer and, upon written notice to M&I, its Affiliates, and made transferable to Customer's successor in a merger or acquisition transaction; all other grant language (term, fee condition, modification right, Article 23 conditions) retained verbatim.
2. § 23.5(1) — the retained no-transfer/no-sublicence covenant conformed with "other than as permitted by Section 23.4" so it does not contradict the new grant.

Preferred-level items (perpetuity/irrevocability, contractors, breach-only termination) were deliberately not pursued, as they would require rewriting this term-limited, release-event-conditioned escrow licence; this is noted in the rationale rather than drafted.
